help.victoryFallback: Conditions appear here once the match begins.
help.victoryDeadline:
DEADLINE

At the end of {{days}} days with no winner, whoever has the greater progress toward their objectives wins — progress counts partial damage, not just completed conditions. The VICTORY OBJECTIVES panel tracks both sides in real time.
help.fases:
TURN STRUCTURE

Each turn is a day of operations with two periods: ☀ Day and 🌙 Night. Each period has a Movement phase and a Combat phase.

SIMULTANEOUS MOVEMENT

Both sides plan at the same time. The enemy appears at its previous position until both confirm — end with End Movement. Green hexes are the possible steps for the selected unit.

DETECTION AND NIGHT

You only see enemies within your units' detection range (fog of war). At night detection drops (−2), except submarines, which use sonar. Submarines in deep water are harder to detect.

OPERATIONAL DEADLINE

The operation lasts at most 12 days. At the end of that time, whoever has the greater progress toward their objectives wins.
help.combate:
DECLARING ATTACKS

In the combat phase, select a unit and click red targets (detected and in range). Choose the weapon and salvo size, then confirm with Confirm Attacks. Resolution is simultaneous.

COMBAT ROUNDS

Each engagement has up to 2 rounds. After the first, both sides decide to CONTINUE or STOP. Whoever continues alone gains the initiative advantage (rolls 2d6, higher value used). In the second round the defending group counterattacks with short-range weapons.

INTERCEPTION AND GROUPING

Missiles can be intercepted by the target's air defense — ships stacked on the same hex pool their defenses and defend as a group. Torpedoes cannot be intercepted; ASBM is only stopped by BMD.

DAMAGE AND DEGRADATION

Damage reduces SP (staying power). Non-fatal hits also degrade a random subsystem: detection, movement, combat capability, or maximum fuel.
help.logistica:
FUEL POINTS (FP)

Conventional ships and submarines have limited FP. Cost per period: stationary = 1 FP, move 1 hex = 1, 2 hexes = 2, 3+ = 3 (max. 4 FP/turn). Attacking and absorbing damage cost +1 FP each.

0 FP = inoperative unit: cannot move, attack, or defend until refueled.

REFUELING

End the period stacked with a tanker, logistics ship, or friendly port: FP returns to maximum. Nuclear units and FPSOs do not consume FP.

AIRCRAFT

Aircraft have FP = 2× movement and return to base after combat. An airborne aircraft with 0 FP and no base in range is lost. At a base or carrier, it refuels and is ready again next turn.

MUNITIONS

Missiles and torpedoes are finite (see N/N in the panel). Restocking: Blue units stationary in port, aircraft at base, and land units. The Red force does not restock naval weapons at sea — use your salvos wisely.

landing.pageDescription: Exclusion Zone: a turn-based historical naval wargame set in the 1982 Falklands/Malvinas War. Command Argentina or the United Kingdom in hexagonal combat, with a day/night cycle and fog of war. Online multiplayer or against the bot.
landing.ogDescription: Exclusion Zone — South Atlantic, 1982. A turn-based historical naval wargame — Argentina vs. the United Kingdom. Hexagonal combat, day/night cycle, and fog of war. Online multiplayer or against the bot.
landing.twitterDescription: Exclusion Zone — South Atlantic, 1982. A turn-based historical naval wargame — Argentina vs. the United Kingdom. Online multiplayer or against the bot.
landing.conceptBody: A historical naval wargame set in the South Atlantic in 1982, covering the Argentine Patagonian coast, the Falkland/Malvinas Islands, and South Georgia. Two commanders — Argentina (Blue Force, defending the islands) and the United Kingdom (Red Force, the expeditionary task force sailing from Ascension) — contest the maritime theater in turns that represent 12 hours of real combat, inspired by the U.S. Naval War College's War at Sea series.
landing.feat1Body: A real georeferenced chart of the South Atlantic. Each hex represents 75 nautical miles.
landing.feat2Body: Turns alternate between day and night periods. Night reduces detection ranges.
landing.feat3Body: Enemy units are only visible within your forces' detection range.
landing.feat4Body: Both sides declare attacks at the same time. Resolution is simultaneous and realistic.
landing.oobIntro: Each team controls a set of task groups representing real platforms. The counter icons on the board reflect each group's primary type.
landing.blueNote: 31 task groups on the board · defends the already-occupied islands
landing.redNote: 27 task groups on the board · expeditionary task force sailing from Ascension

landing.blueP02: Type 42 + ex-Fletcher/Sumner (Hércules, Sta. Trinidad, Bouchard, Piedrabuena)
landing.blueP06: Coastal patrol, minesweepers, and picket screen
landing.blueP09: ARA Santa Fe + ARA San Luis
landing.blueP11: A-4Q/B/C Skyhawk, Super Étendard, Canberra, Pucará
landing.blueP14: Garrisons at Puerto Argentino, Goose Green, West Falkland, and South Georgia
landing.blueP15: AAA batteries + MM38 Exocet battery (Puerto Argentino)
landing.blueP16: Continental air bases (Rivadavia, San Julián, Gallegos, Grande) + port
landing.step1Body: One player creates the room and shares the 6-letter code with their opponent.
landing.step2Body: Each team moves its units (click a unit → green hexes = range). End the phase when done. The other force moves next.
landing.step3Body: Select one of your units and click detected enemies within range (red hexes) to declare attacks. Confirm when ready.
landing.step4Body: Once both confirm, attacks are resolved at the same time. Destroyed units are removed from the board.
landing.step5Body: Each force has its own objectives: Argentina (Blue) wins by completing 3 of 5 objectives — sinking the carrier, the logistics ships, the amphibious group, the nuclear submarine, or degrading the British squadron; the United Kingdom (Red) wins by completing its 2, both restricted to the islands theater — Britain operated under rules of engagement that forbade attacks on the Argentine mainland — degrading the local air/naval presence (Pucará, patrols, minesweepers) and the islands' garrison. At the end of 8 days of operations, whoever has the greater progress wins. The game alternates day and night periods.

Every turn has 2 phases — both players act simultaneously.
Movement first: plan your routes and confirm. Then combat resolves the attacks.
